description: The figure presents three pie charts labeled “easy,” “medium,” and “hard,” showing the distribution of four CoT categories across difficulty levels, with a total of 4 slices in each pie and a legend on the right mapping colors to labels (teal = N+K+, olive/yellow = N−K+, tan/brown = N−K−, and reddish-brown = N+K−); each slice contains an internal percentage label and none of the slices appear exploded or otherwise emphasized. In the “easy” chart, N−K+ (olive/yellow) is about 45.9%, N+K+ (teal) about 40.6%, N−K− (tan/brown) about 10.1%, and N+K− (reddish-brown) about 3.3%. In the “medium” chart, N+K+ (teal) is about 44.6%, N−K+ (olive/yellow) about 44.3%, N−K− (tan/brown) about 7.2%, and N+K− (reddish-brown) about 3.9%. In the “hard” chart, N−K− (tan/brown) is about 36.8%, N−K+ (olive/yellow) about 36.2%, N+K+ (teal) about 20.1%, and N+K− (reddish-brown) about 7.0%; the slice ordering appears to follow the circular layout rather than a consistent descending-size order across charts.
